title: Override the airlock manifest
hint: Manifest records are addressed by ID right in the URL. What stops you from typing one that isn't yours?

title: Read another crew member's roster entry
hint: Each crew profile page surfaces sensitive details. The URL tells you which crew member you're looking at — what if it didn't have to be yours?

title: Exfiltrate the full manifest ledger with a stolen station key
hint: Manifest export accepts a token in place of a session. Not every token opens the same doors — find one that opens more than yours.

title: Tamper with the cart submission
hint: The checkout form carries more than just your item choices. Inspect what gets posted back before you trust it to be read-only.

title: Scan an external beacon URL
hint: The bridge will fetch any URL you hand it. Pick one a public client could never reach directly.

title: Reach the cloud metadata endpoint
hint: Cloud hosts expose information only to themselves at a well-known link-local address. The scanner doesn't filter where it goes.

title: Bounce the beacon at the admin loopback
hint: Some admin tooling binds to the loopback interface on purpose. The scanner sees what the public network cannot.

title: Escape the avatar drop zone
hint: Avatar uploads are saved using the filename the client sends. The drop zone is one directory — but what does the filesystem think when the name has a few extra dots and slashes?

cwe.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

title: Pry open the diagnostics panel
hint: Engineering left a tool behind that should have been pulled before launch. Common ops-style paths are worth trying in your address bar.

title: Sign in with default station credentials
hint: Factory-default service accounts get baked into vendor docs and quietly never rotated. Try the credentials a manual would ship with.

title: Trigger a verbose telemetry dump
hint: Crash an endpoint with malformed input and see what the server volunteers about itself in the response.

cwe.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

title: Salvage from a deprecated image parser
hint: Avatar uploads pass through a parser whose advisories were never patched. The relevant CVE is public — find it.

title: Exploit the known JWT library flaw
hint: Some JWT libraries trust the token's own header more than they should. Inspect the algorithm field and ask what it would take to skip verification entirely.

title: Leverage the vulnerable markdown renderer
hint: The comms log's markdown renderer is years behind. Public bypasses exist for that version — find one that slips past its sanitizer.

title: Crack the comms beacon cipher
hint: The outbound signing routine isn't a textbook algorithm — and a short, guessable secret makes brittle crypto.

cwe.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

title: Decode the remember-me beacon token
hint: Convenience features sometimes trade safety for ease. Look closely at what the 'remember me' option leaves behind in your browser.

cwe.name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in a Cookie

title: Reverse a legacy crew password hash
hint: Older crew records were never migrated to modern password storage. If you can find them, the rest is a familiar offline exercise.

cwe.name: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

title: Spike the requisition query
hint: The commissary search bar reaches the database directly. What happens when your query carries more than just words?

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

title: Slip past the badge reader
hint: The badge reader trusts what you type more than it should. With the right input, the comparison becomes vacuously true.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

title: Inject a payload into the comms log
hint: Comms entries are shown to other crew. When the renderer doesn't escape, what they see is whatever you wrote.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

title: Smuggle script through a crew avatar
hint: Crew profile pages render avatars inline for styling control. Some image formats are also documents — and documents can carry more than pixels.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

title: Race the supply allocation gate
hint: The allocation gate reads, decides, then writes. Two requests arriving close enough together might both pass the gate.

title: Reuse a password-reset token
hint: A reset token should be one-shot. Try using one twice and see whether the system actually notices.

cwe.name: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

title: Replay a single-use ration voucher
hint: Vouchers are checked for validity but not necessarily for prior use. Once a code passes, what stops you from passing it again?

title: Hijack a session via fixation
hint: A login should hand you a fresh session identifier. Check what your cookie looks like before and after — and what that implies.

title: Brute-force a crew password
hint: The badge reader doesn't seem to mind repeated wrong guesses. Patience and a list of common passwords go a long way.

cwe.name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

title: Register with a trivial passphrase
hint: The registration form's password rules are forgiving. Try the sort of password every security guide tells you never to use.

title: Tamper with a cargo ledger import
hint: Bulk imports take whatever they're handed. Between the source and the ledger there's nothing checking that the file is genuine.

title: Pry open the unsafe deserialization path
hint: An import endpoint reconstructs runtime objects from input you control. Crafted payloads can do more than just populate fields.

title: Slip a forged update through the patch channel
hint: The patch channel pulls binaries without verifying who sent them. Whoever sits in the middle of that fetch controls what arrives.

cwe.name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check

title: Wipe the comms log trail
hint: Take a destructive action against a comms entry and then go looking for evidence it ever happened.

title: Perform a privileged action with no trace
hint: Sensitive actions should record who did what. Exercise one and see whether anything actually gets written.

title: Forge a log entry via injection
hint: User input lands in the log verbatim. The right control character in the right field can make a forged line look real.

title: Provoke an unchecked exception that leaks state
hint: Some code paths assume input is well-formed. Hand them something that isn't and see what the resulting failure reveals.

cwe.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

title: Force an authorization check to fail open
hint: When a permission check errors out, the safe answer is 'deny.' Find a check whose error path lets you through instead.

title: Exploit a partially-rolled-back transaction
hint: Multi-step operations should be atomic. Crash one mid-flight and see what state the system is left in.
